title: Arms Sales Notification
items_summary: Three MH-60R Multi-mission Helicopters with embedded GPS/INS navigation systems, digital magnetic anomaly detection systems, and associated non-MDE equipment, engines, support, and training.
major_defense_equipment: Eight (8) Embedded Global Positioning System/Precise Positioning Service/Inertial Navigation Systems with Selective Availability/Anti-Spoofing Module (6 installed, 2 spares)
Three (3) Digital Magnetic Anomaly Detection Systems
summary: The Government of Denmark has requested to buy three MH-60R multi-mission helicopters, eight embedded GPS/INS navigation units, and three digital magnetic anomaly detection systems, along with engines, radios, sensors, support, and training, for an estimated total of $425 million ($336 million MDE). The sale is justified as strengthening a NATO Ally's homeland defense and critical infrastructure protection, and Denmark already operates this aircraft, so it can absorb the articles without difficulty and without altering the regional military balance. Transmittal 26-96 is the only transmittal in this notice.

DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE

Arms Sales Notification

AGENCY: Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Department of 
Defense (DoD).

ACTION: Arms sales notice.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

[[Page 75311]]

SUMMARY: The DoD (referred to herein as ``the Department,'' 
``Department of War'' or ``DoW'') is publishing the unclassified text 
of an arms sales notification.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Urooj Zahra at (703) 695-6233, 
[email protected], or [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 36(b) arms sales notification is 
published to fulfill the requirements of section 155 of Public Law 104-
164 dated July 21, 1996. The following is a copy of the attached 
Transmittal 26-96, Policy Justification, and Sensitivity of Technology.

    Dated: November 17, 2026.
Stephanie J. Bost,
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.
Transmittal No. 26-96
Notice of Proposed Issuance Letter of Offer Pursuant to Section 
36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act, as amended
    (i) Prospective Purchaser: Government of Denmark
    (ii) Total Estimated Value:

Major Defense Equipment*................  $336 million
Other...................................  $ 89 million
                                         -------------------------------
  TOTAL.................................  $425 million
 

    (iii) Description and Quantity or Quantities of Articles or 
Services under Consideration for Purchase:

Major Defense Equipment (MDE):
    Three (3) MH-60R Multi-mission Helicopters
    Eight (8) Embedded Global Positioning System/Precise Positioning 
Service/Inertial Navigation Systems with Selective Availability/Anti-
Spoofing Module (6 installed, 2 spares)
    Three (3) Digital Magnetic Anomaly Detection Systems
Non-MDE:
    The following non-MDE items will also be included: T700-GE-401D 
engines; M514 impulse cartridge/cartridge actuated devices; MJ20 
cartridge actuated thruster/cartridge actuated devices; WB53 fire 
extinguisher cartridge/cartridge actuated devices; CCU-136A/A impulse 
cartridges; AN/ARC-210 RT-2036 radios with communications security; AN/
AAR-47 missile warning systems; AN/APX-128 identification friend or foe 
transponders; AN/ALE-47 dispenser, electronic countermeasures; advanced 
data transfer systems; AN/AAS-44C(V) multi-spectral targeting systems; 
identification friend or foe mode 4/5 cryptographic applique, KIV-79; 
joint mission planning systems; AN/ALQ-210 electronic support measures 
systems; APS-153(V) multi-mode radars; spare engine containers; spare 
and repair parts; support and test equipment; communications equipment; 
ferry support; publications and technical documentation; U.S. 
Government and contractor engineering, technical, and logistics support 
services; and other related elements of logistics and program support.

    (iv) Military Department: Navy (DE-P-SBD)
    (v) Prior Related Cases, if any: (DE-P-SAE); (DE-P-GBP)
    (vi) Sales Commission, Fee, etc., Paid, Offered, or Agreed to be 
Paid: None known at this Time
    (vii) Sensitivity of Technology Contained in the Defense Article or 
Defense Services Proposed to be Sold: See Attached Annex
    (viii) Date Report Delivered to Congress: September 22, 2026
    * as defined in Section 47(6) of the Arms Export Control Act.

POLICY JUSTIFICATION

Denmark--MH-60R Multi Mission Helicopters

    The Government of Denmark has requested to buy three (3) MH-60R 
multi-mission helicopters; eight (8) embedded global positioning 
system/precise positioning service/inertial navigation systems with 
selective availability/anti-spoofing module (6 installed, 2 spares); 
and three (3) digital magnetic anomaly detection systems. The following 
non-major defense equipment items will also be included: T700-GE-401D 
engines; M514 impulse cartridge/cartridge actuated devices; MJ20 
cartridge actuated thruster/cartridge actuated devices; WB53 fire 
extinguisher cartridge/cartridge actuated devices; CCU-136A/A impulse 
cartridges; AN/ARC-210 RT-2036 radios with communications security; AN/
AAR-47 missile warning systems; AN/APX-128 identification friend or foe 
transponders; AN/ALE-47 dispenser, electronic countermeasures; advanced 
data transfer systems; AN/AAS-44C(V) multi-spectral targeting systems; 
identification friend or foe Mode 4/5 cryptographic applique, KIV-79; 
joint mission planning systems; AN/ALQ-210 electronic support measures 
systems; APS-153(V) multi-mode radars; spare engine containers; spare 
and repair parts; support and test equipment; communications equipment; 
ferry support; publications and technical documentation; personnel 
training; U.S. Government and contractor engineering, technical, and 
logistics support services; obsolescence engineering, integration, and 
test activities required to ensure readiness for the production of the 
Denmark MH-60R helicopters and other related elements of logistics and 
program support. The estimated total cost is $425 million.
    This proposed sale will support the foreign policy goals and 
national security objectives of the United States by improving the 
security of a NATO Ally that is a force for political stability and 
economic progress in Europe.
    The proposed sale will improve Denmark's capability to meet current 
and future threats by providing increased security for its critical 
infrastructure. Denmark will use the enhanced capability to strengthen 
its homeland defense. Denmark will have no difficulty absorbing these 
articles and services into its armed forces as they are currently 
operating this aircraft.
    The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the 
basic military balance in the region.
    The principal contractors will be Lockheed Martin, located in 
Owego, NY, and Sikorsky, Corporation, located in Stratford, CT. At this 
time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed 
in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be 
defined in negotiations between the purchaser and the contractor.
    Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the 
assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor 
representatives to Denmark.
    There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a 
result of this proposed sale.
Transmittal No. 26-96
Notice of Proposed Issuance of Letter of Offer Pursuant to Section 
36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act
Annex
Item No. vii
    (vii) Sensitivity of Technology:
    1. The MH-60R multi-mission helicopter focuses primarily on anti-
submarine and anti surface warfare missions. The MH-60R also performs 
search and rescue, naval gunfire support, surveillance, communications 
relay, logistics support, personnel transfer, and vertical 
replenishment missions. The MH-60R carries several sensors and data 
links to enhance its ability to work in a network centric battle group 
and as an extension of its home ship/main operating base. The mission 
equipment subsystem consists

[[Page 75312]]

of the following sensors and subsystems: an acoustics system capable of 
dipping sonar and sonobuoy operations, Multi-Mode Radar (MMR) with 
integral Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) interrogator, radios with 
communications security (COMSEC), Electronic Support Measures, 
Integrated Self-Defense, and Multi-Spectral Targeting System. The 
aircraft processes sensor data onboard and transmits data via Common 
Data Link (also referred to as Hawklink). The aircraft is compatible 
with night vision. It can carry AGM-114A/B/K/N/R Hellfire missiles, as 
well as MK 46/54 torpedoes to engage surface and sub-surface targets.
    a. AN/ARC-210 RT-2036(C) Radio. The RT-2036(C) radios are capable 
of line of sight and beyond line of sight and can transmit clear or 
secure voice using Single Channel Ground and Airborne Radio System or 
HAVEQUICK security features. The ultra-high frequency/very high 
frequency radios (ARC-210) contain embedded sensitive encryption 
algorithms and keying material.
    b. The Embedded Global Positioning System -Inertial Navigation 
System LN-100G/M is a sensor that combines GPS and inertial sensor 
inputs to provide accurate location information for navigation and 
targeting.
    c. Advanced Digital Antenna Production (ADAP), antenna electronics. 
The ADAP antenna electronics interfaces with the ADAP Controlled 
Reception Pattern antenna antennas to ensure availability of GPS 
signals to the aircraft.
    d. AN/APX-128 IFF Transponder, Digital. The IFF AN/APX-128 
transponder is capable of both Mode 5 and Mode S secure modes and 
provides own ship positional information.
    e. KIV-79 IFF Mode 4/5 Cryptographic Applique. The KIV-79 is Type 1 
NSA-certified COMSEC for IFF. The KIV-79 provides cryptographic and 
time-of-day services, concurrent Mode 4/5 operations as well as 
concurrent interrogator/transponder operations. The KIV-79 IFF system 
is deployed to identify cooperative, friendly systems.
    f. Acoustics Algorithms are used to process dipping sonar and 
sonobuoy data for target tracking and for the acoustics mission 
planner, which is a tactical aid employed to optimize the deployment of 
sonobuoys and the dipping sonar (dipping sonar was procured during the 
initial buy of the MH-60Rs).
    g. The AN/APS-153 MMR with an integrated IFF and inverse synthetic 
aperture provides target surveillance/detection capability.
    h. Digital Magnetic Anomaly Detection capability is being 
introduced into the MH-60R in response to a fleet need for a submarine 
detection capability which will be effective in acoustically harsh 
environments.
    i. Advanced Data Transfer System with Type 1 Encryption for data at 
rest.
    j. AN/ALQ-210 electronic support measures system identifies the 
location of an emitter.
    2. The highest level of classification of defense articles, 
components, and services included in this potential sale is SECRET
    3. If a technologically advanced adversary were to obtain knowledge 
of the specific hardware and software elements, the information could 
be used to develop countermeasures that might reduce system 
effectiveness or be used in the development of a system with similar or 
advanced capabilities.
    4. A determination has been made that Denmark can provide 
substantially the same degree of protection for the sensitive 
technology being released as the U.S. Government. This proposed sale is 
necessary in furtherance of the U.S. foreign policy and national 
security objectives outlined in the Policy Justification.
    5. All defense articles and services listed in this transmittal 
have been authorized for release and export to the Government of 
Denmark.
